name: Ertugliflozin
mechanism: Selective SGLT2 inhibitor - blocks renal glucose reabsorption in proximal tubule, increases urinary glucose excretion (30-50g/day), reduces blood glucose independent of insulin
dosing: T2DM: 5mg OD initially, increase to 15mg OD if tolerated and needed for glycaemic control. Take morning with/without food. eGFR <45: do not initiate (stop if falls below 45). Available with metformin (Segluromet) or sitagliptin (Steglujan)
contraindications: Type 1 diabetes, DKA, eGFR persistently <45 ml/min/1.73m², dialysis. Caution: elderly (volume depletion risk), recurrent UTIs, genital infection history, at risk of DKA
interactions: Diuretics, ACE inhibitors/ARBs ↑ volume depletion risk. Insulin/sulfonylureas ↑ hypoglycaemia (reduce doses). May ↑ lithium excretion. Interferes with 1,5-AG assay
monitoring: eGFR before starting and annually (more if CKD stage 3a/3b). HbA1c 3-monthly. BP. Volume status (especially elderly/on diuretics). Ketones if unwell (DKA risk). Genital/UTI symptoms. Foot checks (Fournier's gangrene risk rare)
pregnancy: Avoid - limited data. May affect fetal kidney development. Use insulin for diabetes in pregnancy. Stop when pregnancy planned/confirmed
sideEffects: Very common: genital mycotic infections (women 10-15%, men 3-4% - treat with topical antifungal), UTIs. Common: volume depletion (dizziness, postural hypotension especially elderly/on diuretics), hypoglycaemia (with insulin/SU). Rare: DKA (euglycaemic DKA possible - ketones despite normal glucose), Fournier's gangrene (necrotizing fasciitis of perineum - emergency), lower limb amputation (possible ↑ risk), acute kidney injury
pharmacokinetics: Well absorbed, peak 1h. Half-life: 17h. Minimal renal excretion unchanged (<2%), mainly metabolized (UGT) and excreted in faeces. Unlike some SGLT2is, doesn't accumulate in renal impairment but less effective
clinicalPearls: Newer SGLT2i with similar efficacy to empagliflozin/dapagliflozin. Cardiovascular/renal outcomes data less extensive than empa/dapa. Weight loss 2-3kg average. Modest BP reduction (3-5mmHg). Low intrinsic hypoglycaemia risk. Counsel about genital hygiene, adequate hydration. Stop during acute illness/surgery (DKA risk - especially if insulin dose reduced inappropriately). Sick day rules essential: stop if vomiting/unable to eat, check ketones. Higher genital infection rate than some SGLT2is. Consider if HbA1c inadequate on metformin or GLP-1 agonist. Not currently licensed for heart failure/CKD indications (unlike empa/dapa)
indication: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (monotherapy if metformin not tolerated, or add-on therapy)
